components.name: agent
components.purpose: Renders an agent's configuration card — name, model, instructions, tool roster, and output schema — so a user can see what the agent is before or while it runs.
essential_behavior: AgentTools is an accordion: each AgentTool collapses to a one-line description and expands to reveal that tool's inputSchema
AgentInstructions renders its string child as markdown, not plain text
AgentOutput renders the output schema as syntax-highlighted code
AgentHeader shows the model identifier as a distinct badge from the agent name

browser_artifacts.artifact: Shiki syntax highlighting for AgentOutput schema
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Shiki emits themed HTML spans; there is no DOM to hydrate in RN
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Use a tokenizer that emits <Text> runs, or accept monospace-plus-color-by-token-type

state_contract.context_published: none of its own; AgentTools relies on Accordion's context
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: AgentTool takes an AI SDK `Tool` object ({ description, inputSchema }). No message parts.

components.name: artifact
components.purpose: A framed container for a discrete generated deliverable (a document, a code file, a rendered output) that sits beside or above the transcript rather than inside a bubble.
essential_behavior: Header stays fixed while ArtifactContent scrolls independently of the transcript
ArtifactAction is icon-plus-tooltip; the label is not visible until hover on web
ArtifactClose dismisses the artifact without unmounting the conversation behind it

browser_artifacts.artifact: Tooltip-on-hover for ArtifactAction labels
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: There is no hover on touch; a tooltip that only appears on hover is an invisible label on mobile
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Show the label inline, or use icon + short text; do not port hover-only affordances

browser_artifacts.artifact: Side-by-side / split-pane placement next to the transcript
browser_artifacts.port_advice: On phone this is a full-screen sheet or a pushed route, not a side panel

state_contract.context_published: none — pure layout shell
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: none; you decide what an artifact is from your own tool output

components.name: attachments
components.purpose: Displays files and referenced sources attached to a message or staged in the composer, with previews and per-item removal.
essential_behavior: Three layout variants — grid, inline, list — that change density, not content
AttachmentPreview branches on media category: image thumbnail, video poster, or a type icon fallback
AttachmentRemove is revealed on hover over the item on web, and calls the per-item onRemove
getMediaCategory(attachment) classifies into image|video|audio|document|source|unknown; getAttachmentLabel falls back to 'Image'/'Attachment' when there is no filename

browser_artifacts.artifact: Hover-revealed remove button
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: No hover state on touch — the remove control would be permanently invisible
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Always-visible small X, or long-press/swipe-to-remove

browser_artifacts.artifact: AttachmentHoverCard full-size preview on hover
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Tap-to-open a modal preview; the hovercard subtree can be dropped entirely

browser_artifacts.artifact: CSS grid auto-fill for the grid variant
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: RN flexbox has no grid auto-placement
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Fixed-column flex wrap computed from container width

browser_artifacts.artifact: blob: object URLs for local previews
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Use the file:// URI from the picker; see the prompt-input blob→data rule

state_contract.context_published: Attachment publishes the current attachment record to its children
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: AI SDK `FileUIPart` and `SourceDocumentUIPart` shapes (mediaType, filename, url)

components.name: audio-player
components.purpose: Plays a generated or referenced audio clip with transport controls, scrubbing, and volume — the surface for TTS output.
essential_behavior: Accepts either a remote URL (src) or an AI SDK speech result and builds a data: URL from base64 + mediaType
Seek buttons jump by seekOffset seconds (default 10) rather than to an absolute position
Time display and duration display are separate slots so a compact bar can drop one
Scrubbing the time range seeks without restarting playback

browser_artifacts.artifact: media-chrome Web Components (MediaController, MediaPlayButton, MediaTimeRange…)
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Custom Elements registry does not exist in RN
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Rebuild the whole control bar over expo-audio/react-native-track-player; only the slot names and seekOffset semantics survive

browser_artifacts.artifact: data:audio/mpeg;base64 src on an <audio> element
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: RN audio players generally will not stream a huge base64 data URI
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Write the base64 to a cache file and play the file:// URI

browser_artifacts.artifact: Volume slider
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Mobile OSes own volume via hardware keys; in-app volume sliders are an anti-pattern on iOS
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Drop the volume range; keep mute

state_contract.context_published: MediaController context consumed by every control (web-component context, not React context)
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: AI SDK speech `Result` shape (base64 + mediaType) from generateSpeech

components.name: canvas
components.purpose: An infinite pan/zoom workspace for rendering an agent's graph — nodes, edges, and their connections — as a spatial diagram.

shadcn_primitives: none directly — it is @xyflow/react's ReactFlow with AI-oriented defaults

essential_behavior: Pan on scroll, selection on drag, auto-fit on mount, delete keys bound, double-click zoom disabled, pan-on-drag disabled
Registers edgeTypes/nodeTypes maps so nodes and edges are pluggable components
Children (Controls, Panel) render as overlays positioned above the graph, not in graph coordinates

browser_artifacts.artifact: @xyflow/react (React Flow) entirely
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: React Flow is DOM+SVG: absolutely positioned divs with CSS transform matrices, SVG edge paths, wheel/pointer events, ResizeObserver, and getBoundingClientRect-based node measurement
browser_artifacts.port_advice: There is no drop-in. Rebuild on react-native-gesture-handler (pinch/pan) + reanimated (transform) + react-native-svg (edges), or cut canvas from the port and revisit as its own project

browser_artifacts.artifact: Scroll-wheel pan and keyboard delete bindings
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: No wheel events, no hardware Delete key on phone
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Pinch-zoom, two-finger pan, long-press-to-delete

browser_artifacts.artifact: DOM measurement for node sizing and auto-fit
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: getBoundingClientRect has no RN equivalent; onLayout is async and per-view
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Require explicit node dimensions, or accumulate onLayout before computing fit

state_contract.context_published: React Flow's internal store (useReactFlow), consumed by Controls/Panel/Toolbar/Node handles
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: none — you map your own agent graph into node/edge arrays

components.name: chain-of-thought
components.purpose: A collapsible stepwise trace of the model's reasoning, richer than plain reasoning text: each step has a status, and steps can carry search results and images.
essential_behavior: Steps render as a vertical timeline: each has an icon (default a dot), a label, an optional description, and a status that changes the icon/color
Search results render as a wrapped row of badges under their step
ChainOfThoughtImage takes an optional caption below the image
Collapsed by default; header is the trigger

browser_artifacts.artifact: CSS pseudo-element connector line between timeline steps
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Render an explicit 1px View as the rail, or a per-step left border View

browser_artifacts.artifact: Sub-components throw outside <ChainOfThought>
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Not browser-specific, but it is a hard composition law worth preserving
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Keep the throwing context — it catches à-la-carte misuse at dev time

state_contract.context_published: ChainOfThought context — sub-components throw with 'ChainOfThought components must be used within ChainOfThought'
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: not a first-class AI SDK part; you derive steps from your own agent events

components.name: checkpoint
components.purpose: Marks a restorable point in the conversation so the user can rewind the transcript to that message.
essential_behavior: Renders as a horizontal rule through the transcript with the icon/label centered on it — it reads as a divider, not a message
The trigger's action is destructive-ish: it truncates the message array (setMessages(messages.slice(0, i + 1)))
Default icon is a bookmark; the whole row is inline between messages

browser_artifacts.artifact: Separator line rendered behind centered content via absolute positioning / flex with border
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Row of [flex-1 hairline View][content][flex-1 hairline View] — trivially portable

browser_artifacts.artifact: Hover tooltip on the restore trigger
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Visible label; and confirm before truncating, since a mistap loses transcript

state_contract.context_published: none
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: consumes the useChat `messages` array and calls `setMessages` — this is the one component that mutates chat state

components.name: code-block
components.purpose: Renders a fenced code block with syntax highlighting, an optional filename header, line numbers, and a copy button — the single most common non-prose thing an LLM emits.
essential_behavior: Syntax highlighting per BundledLanguage; unknown languages degrade to plain monospace instead of erroring
Copy button flips to a check icon for ~2000ms then reverts (timeout prop)
Copy failure calls onError rather than silently doing nothing
Optional line numbers in a non-selectable gutter
Long lines scroll horizontally; they do not wrap

browser_artifacts.artifact: Shiki-generated HTML (nested <span> with inline styles) inside <pre><code>
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Emits an HTML string; there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML equivalent for RN text
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Use Shiki's token API (codeToTokens) and map tokens to <Text> children — the highlighting theme survives, the HTML does not

browser_artifacts.artifact: navigator.clipboard.writeText
browser_artifacts.port_advice: expo-clipboard; keep the same onCopy/onError/timeout contract

browser_artifacts.artifact: Horizontal overflow scroll on <pre>
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Horizontal ScrollView per block; watch nesting inside the vertical transcript scroller

browser_artifacts.artifact: user-select:none on the line-number gutter
browser_artifacts.port_advice: selectable={false} on the gutter Text

state_contract.context_published: CodeBlock publishes { code, language } so CodeBlockCopyButton needs no props
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: indirect — MessageResponse's markdown renderer routes fenced blocks here

components.name: commit
components.purpose: Renders a git commit an agent made or is proposing — message, hash, author, timestamp, and the changed-file list with +/- counts.
essential_behavior: Collapsed shows message + metadata; expanded reveals the file list
CommitFileStatus maps to a single letter and color: added=A green, modified=M yellow, deleted=D red, renamed=R blue
CommitTimestamp renders a relative time ('2 hours ago') by default from a Date
CommitCopyButton copies the hash, not the message

browser_artifacts.artifact: <time> semantic element
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Plain Text; keep the relative-time formatting

browser_artifacts.artifact: Clipboard API for hash copy
browser_artifacts.port_advice: expo-clipboard

browser_artifacts.artifact: Monospace path truncation with CSS text-overflow ellipsis in the middle
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: CSS ellipsis is end-only anyway; middle-truncation is a JS hack
browser_artifacts.port_advice: numberOfLines={1} ellipsizeMode='middle' — RN actually does this better than the web

state_contract.context_published: Commit publishes the commit record so CommitMessage/CommitHash can default from it
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: none — driven by your own tool output

components.name: confirmation
components.purpose: The human-in-the-loop gate: renders a tool's approval request with Accept/Reject, then the resolved outcome. Without it a gated agent silently stalls.
essential_behavior: Renders NOTHING when there is no approval object, or when state is input-streaming / input-available — the first child is null
ConfirmationActions only renders in the approval-requested state; after a response the buttons disappear
ConfirmationAccepted shows only when approval.approved === true; ConfirmationRejected only when false
Responding calls back into the chat with { id: approval.id, approved: boolean }

browser_artifacts.artifact: none of substance — this is layout plus a state machine
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Port as-is; it is one of the highest-value/lowest-risk components in the set

state_contract.context_published: Confirmation publishes { approval, state } to its children — sub-components branch on it
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: AI SDK tool-part `state` plus the approval record; response goes to addToolApprovalResponse({ id, approved })

components.name: connection
components.purpose: Draws the in-flight line while a user drags a new edge between two node handles on a canvas.

subcomponents: Connection (single component, used as React Flow's connectionLineComponent)

essential_behavior: Animated bezier from the source handle to the pointer, with a circle marker at the pointer end
Takes fromX/fromY/toX/toY plus fromPosition/toPosition, and connectionStatus (valid/invalid/null) to color the line

browser_artifacts.artifact: SVG <path> with a computed bezier and SMIL/CSS animation, rendered into React Flow's connection layer
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: It is an SVG child of the React Flow renderer and receives pointer coordinates from DOM events
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Only meaningful if canvas is rebuilt. Then: react-native-svg Path + reanimated shared values fed by a PanGesture

browser_artifacts.artifact: Pointer coordinates in viewport space
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Gesture handler absoluteX/absoluteY translated into canvas space

state_contract.context_published: none — it is a render-prop slot for React Flow
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: none

components.name: context
components.purpose: Shows how much of the model's context window the conversation has consumed, broken down by input/output/reasoning/cached tokens, with estimated cost.
essential_behavior: Trigger is a compact percentage + icon; the breakdown lives behind a hover card
Each usage row renders NOTHING when its token count is zero — a model with no reasoning tokens shows no reasoning row
Token counts use Intl.NumberFormat compact notation: exact below 1000, then K / M / B
Cost is computed via tokenlens from modelId and only appears when modelId is supplied
Header shows a progress bar of usedTokens / maxTokens

browser_artifacts.artifact: HoverCard as the disclosure mechanism
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Hover has no touch equivalent; on mobile the entire breakdown would be unreachable
browser_artifacts.port_advice: RNR has hover-card but on touch it needs press-to-open; consider a bottom sheet or popover instead

browser_artifacts.artifact: Intl.NumberFormat compact notation
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Hermes ships a reduced Intl; compact notation support varies
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Verify on Hermes with the intl polyfill, or hand-roll the K/M/B formatter

state_contract.context_published: Context publishes usage/maxTokens/modelId; ContextTrigger throws with 'Context components must be used within Context'
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: AI SDK `LanguageModelUsage` ({ inputTokens, outputTokens, reasoningTokens, cachedInputTokens }) off the finished response

components.name: controls
components.purpose: The zoom-in / zoom-out / fit-view / lock cluster for a canvas.
essential_behavior: Four togglable buttons: showZoom, showFitView, showInteractive, plus position
Acts on the React Flow viewport store, not on any prop you pass

browser_artifacts.artifact: Depends on React Flow's useReactFlow store for zoomIn/zoomOut/fitView
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: That store does not exist without the DOM renderer
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Only ships if canvas ships; then wire to your reanimated scale/translate shared values

browser_artifacts.artifact: Discrete zoom buttons as the primary zoom affordance
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Pinch is the primary gesture on mobile; fit-view is the only button worth keeping

state_contract.context_published: none; consumes React Flow context
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: none

components.name: conversation
components.purpose: The transcript scroller — keeps the newest message visible while streaming without fighting a user who has scrolled up to read history.
essential_behavior: Sticks to the bottom as content streams in, and RELEASES stickiness the moment the user scrolls up — it must never yank a reader back down mid-token
ConversationScrollButton renders ONLY while not at the bottom; pressing it calls scrollToBottom()
ConversationEmptyState occupies the scroller when messages is empty (title/description/icon/children)
ConversationDownload serializes messages to Markdown via messagesToMarkdown(messages, formatMessage?) and hands the user a file
Content grows from the bottom — a two-message conversation sits at the bottom of the viewport, not the top

browser_artifacts.artifact: use-stick-to-bottom, which does ResizeObserver + scrollHeight/scrollTop math on a div
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: No ResizeObserver; RN scroll metrics come from onScroll/onContentSizeChange events, and scroll position is async
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Rebuild on FlatList inverted, or ScrollView + onContentSizeChange + a nearBottom threshold. This is the single highest-risk behavior in the whole port and deserves its own task

browser_artifacts.artifact: Non-virtualized DOM list (the browser tolerates hundreds of message divs)
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: The DOM is cheap enough that the web version never had to virtualize; RN mounting 500 message views is a memory cliff
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Use FlatList/FlashList from day one. The prior RN port shipped a ScrollView + .map() and its own KB flags this as the defect most likely to ship unnoticed

browser_artifacts.artifact: Blob + anchor download for ConversationDownload
browser_artifacts.port_advice: expo-file-system write + expo-sharing share sheet

browser_artifacts.artifact: No keyboard handling (the browser resizes the viewport)
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: n/a — it is a missing behavior, not an artifact
browser_artifacts.port_advice: The RN version MUST add KeyboardAvoidingView + safe-area insets; the web component has nothing to copy here

state_contract.context_published: StickToBottom context: { isAtBottom, scrollToBottom } consumed by ConversationScrollButton
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: ConversationDownload takes `UIMessage[]`; the scroller itself is content-agnostic

components.name: edge
components.purpose: The line between two canvas nodes — either a dashed preview or a solid line with a dot animating along it to show data flow.
essential_behavior: Temporary: dashed bezier in the ring color, for preview/proposed connections
Animated: solid path with a circle traversing it on a 2-second infinite loop — the loop is the whole point (it reads as 'data is moving')
Registered by name in the canvas edgeTypes map; requires a const assertion on the type map or TypeScript widens it

browser_artifacts.artifact: SVG <path> with getBezierPath from @xyflow/react plus SMIL/CSS keyframe animation
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: SVG path + CSS animation in the React Flow SVG layer
browser_artifacts.port_advice: react-native-svg Path + reanimated withRepeat along a computed path; there is no getBezierPath, you compute the control points yourself

browser_artifacts.artifact: markerEnd arrowhead via SVG <marker> defs
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Draw the arrowhead as an explicit Polygon

state_contract.context_published: none
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: none

components.name: environment-variables
components.purpose: Displays a set of env vars an agent needs or set, with values masked by default and a per-var copy in shell-export form.
essential_behavior: Values are MASKED until the toggle is flipped — showing a secret by default is the failure mode this component exists to prevent
Copy emits `export KEY="value"` (copyFormat), not the bare value
Required vars carry a distinct badge
The toggle is global to the group, not per-var

browser_artifacts.artifact: Clipboard API
browser_artifacts.port_advice: expo-clipboard

browser_artifacts.artifact: CSS text-security / monospace bullet masking
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Replace the string with bullets in JS; do not rely on secureTextEntry for non-inputs

browser_artifacts.artifact: Copying a secret to the OS clipboard at all
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Mobile clipboards are shared across apps and surfaced in system UI
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Consider a clipboard clear-after-timeout, and never log the value

state_contract.context_published: EnvironmentVariables publishes showValues; EnvironmentVariable publishes { name, value } so children default from it
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: none

components.name: file-tree
components.purpose: A hierarchical file/folder browser for the workspace an agent is operating on, with independent select and expand.
essential_behavior: CRITICAL: the chevron expands/collapses; the NAME selects. One tap must not do both. This is an explicit, tested law in the web library
Expanded state is a Set<string> of paths — controlled via expanded/onExpandedChange or uncontrolled via defaultExpanded
selectedPath highlights exactly one row across the whole tree
FileTreeActions stops click propagation so an action does not also select the row
Indentation depth is derived from nesting, not from a prop

browser_artifacts.artifact: Hover-revealed FileTreeActions
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Always-visible or long-press context menu

browser_artifacts.artifact: Two distinct hit targets (chevron vs name) inside a ~24px row
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: A mouse can hit an 12px chevron; a finger cannot
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Preserve the semantic split but give each target ≥44pt. If you cannot, pick ONE behavior per tap and expose the other via long-press — do NOT collapse them into 'tap does both'

browser_artifacts.artifact: Deep nesting with horizontal overflow scroll
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Cap indent per level (~12pt) and truncate names; or use a drill-down navigation instead of a tree on phone

state_contract.context_published: FileTree publishes { expanded, selectedPath, onSelect, toggle } to folders and files
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: none — you supply the tree

components.name: image
components.purpose: Renders an image the model generated, from AI SDK's base64 result rather than a URL.
essential_behavior: Builds `data:{mediaType};base64,{base64}` internally — the caller passes the AI SDK result object, not a src
Defaults to max-width 100% / height auto so a 1024px image does not blow out the bubble
alt is a real prop, not optional decoration

browser_artifacts.artifact: data: URI in an src
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: RN Image accepts data URIs but a multi-MB base64 string through the JS bridge is a memory and jank problem
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Write base64 to cache with expo-file-system and pass a file:// uri; keep the same prop shape so callers do not change

browser_artifacts.artifact: CSS max-width:100%; height:auto intrinsic sizing
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: RN Image needs explicit dimensions or resizeMode + a container
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Use aspect ratio from the generation request, or Image.getSize before layout

state_contract.context_published: none
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: AI SDK `Experimental_GeneratedImage` from experimental_generateImage

components.name: inline-citation
components.purpose: A superscript-style citation marker inside prose that reveals the cited sources — title, URL, description, and quoted excerpt — without leaving the message.
essential_behavior: The trigger badge shows a count derived from sources.length, and the hostname of the first source
Multiple sources for one citation are paged through in a carousel with a live 'n/total' index
InlineCitationQuote renders the supporting excerpt, not just the link
The marker sits inline in flowing text without breaking the line box

browser_artifacts.artifact: HoverCard trigger
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Tap opens a bottom sheet; a hover-only citation is unreachable on phone

browser_artifacts.artifact: Embla carousel (transform-based track, drag physics, DOM measurement)
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Horizontal paging FlatList with pagingEnabled; keep the index indicator

browser_artifacts.artifact: Inline placement inside a text run
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: RN cannot place an arbitrary View inline in a Text without a nested <Text> or measured hack
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Render the marker as a pressable <Text> child inside the paragraph Text; a View child will break the line box

state_contract.context_published: carousel context for prev/next/index
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: pairs with AI SDK `source-url` / `source-document` parts (sendSources on the route)

components.name: jsx-preview
components.purpose: Renders JSX the model is streaming as live UI — generative UI where the model authors the markup.
essential_behavior: While isStreaming is true it auto-closes unclosed tags and strips tags cut off mid-attribute, so the preview does not flash between tokens
On a parse error it falls back to the LAST SUCCESSFULLY RENDERED JSX rather than blanking
components map whitelists which component names the JSX may reference; bindings supplies variables
onError surfaces parse failures without unmounting

browser_artifacts.artifact: react-jsx-parser, which parses a JSX string into React elements against an HTML element namespace
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Its default output is DOM intrinsics (div/span/p). RN has no intrinsic elements — an unmapped tag renders nothing
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Every tag must map to an RN component. Either ship a strict allowlist (View/Text/Image/RNR components) and reject everything else, or drop this component. Do not carry over an open-tag parser

browser_artifacts.artifact: Effectively evaluating model-authored markup
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: The web version's blast radius is a div; in an app it is your component tree
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Treat as untrusted input. Allowlist only. This is the highest-security-risk component in the set

state_contract.context_published: JSXPreview publishes parse state; JSXPreviewContent throws with 'JSXPreview components must be used within JSXPreview'
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: consumes a streaming text part that happens to contain JSX

components.name: message
components.purpose: One turn in the transcript — the bubble, its role-based alignment/styling, its markdown body, its per-message actions, and response branching.
essential_behavior: The prop is `from`, NOT `role` — <Message from={message.role}>. Getting this wrong is the most common port error
User messages get a contained bubble with primary background and reverse the row; assistant messages render full-width and unbubbled
MessageResponse children is a STRING of markdown — never React nodes, never AI SDK parts. parseIncompleteMarkdown defaults true so a half-streamed **bold** does not render literal asterisks
MessageBranchSelector hides itself when there is only one branch
MessageAction is icon + tooltip label

browser_artifacts.artifact: Streamdown / remark-gfm / rehype-katex markdown pipeline emitting HTML
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: Produces an HTML tree; tables, task lists, footnotes and KaTeX all assume DOM
browser_artifacts.port_advice: This is the biggest single sub-project. Pick an RN markdown renderer, map every node type to RNR text styles, and decide explicitly whether tables/math ship. Do not assume parity

browser_artifacts.artifact: parseIncompleteMarkdown operating on an HTML-producing parser
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: The algorithm is renderer-agnostic; the integration is not
browser_artifacts.port_advice: KEEP this behavior — without it every streamed message flickers raw syntax. Port the incomplete-token logic into whatever renderer you choose

browser_artifacts.artifact: Hover-revealed MessageActions
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Always-visible action row under assistant messages, or long-press menu

browser_artifacts.artifact: max-width via CSS ch/percentage on prose
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Percentage of container width; bubbles should not span full width on tablet

state_contract.context_published: Message publishes { from }; MessageBranch publishes branch index — MessageBranchNext throws with 'MessageBranch components must be used within MessageBranch'
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: AI SDK `UIMessage` (NOT the removed `ConversationMessage` type); you switch over message.parts and route text parts to MessageResponse

components.name: mic-selector
components.purpose: Lets the user pick which microphone the voice input uses, listing the OS's available audio input devices.
essential_behavior: Opening the selector without mic permission triggers the permission request — the device list is empty until permission is granted
MicSelectorList is a render-prop over MediaDeviceInfo[]
MicSelectorLabel strips the trailing '(XXXX:XXXX)' hardware IDs browsers append to device labels
Trigger measures its own width so the popover matches it

browser_artifacts.artifact: navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices() + getUserMedia({audio:true})
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: There is no RN API that enumerates audio input devices the way the browser does
browser_artifacts.port_advice: iOS/Android do not expose an arbitrary device list to apps; the platform owns routing (AVAudioSession route picker, Bluetooth). This component has no honest native equivalent — either drop it or replace with a system route picker

browser_artifacts.artifact: Hardware-ID label parsing
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: That suffix is a Chrome artifact
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Dead code natively

browser_artifacts.artifact: cmdk Command palette with type-to-filter
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: cmdk is DOM-only and RNR has no command primitive
browser_artifacts.port_advice: If kept, rebuild as bottom sheet + FlatList + TextInput filter

browser_artifacts.artifact: Trigger width measurement via getBoundingClientRect
browser_artifacts.port_advice: onLayout, or just use full-width sheet

state_contract.context_published: MicSelector publishes { devices, value, setValue }; useAudioDevices returns { devices, loading, error, hasPermission, loadDevices }
state_contract.ai_sdk_expectations: none

components.name: model-selector
components.purpose: A searchable command palette for choosing the model, grouped by provider with provider logos and keyboard shortcuts.
essential_behavior: Type-to-filter across all groups, with an explicit empty state when nothing matches
ModelSelectorLogo derives its src from the provider name: https://models.dev/logos/{provider}.svg
Grouped by provider with headings and separators

components.name: transcription
components.purpose: Renders timestamped speech segments synced to audio playback, where tapping a segment seeks the audio to that moment.
essential_behavior: children is a RENDER FUNCTION (segment, index) => ReactNode, not static nodes — you can render TranscriptionSegment or your own markup
Three visual states derived from currentTime: active (currentTime within [startSecond, endSecond]) gets primary color; past gets muted; future gets muted at lower opacity
Tapping a segment calls onSeek(segment.startSecond). With NO onSeek the tap is a no-op and the cursor stays default — it never invents a seek
Segments whose text is empty or whitespace are DROPPED before reaching children
currentTime defaults to 0, so with no controlled time the first segment is active

browser_artifacts.artifact: cursor-pointer vs cursor-default as the affordance that a segment is seekable
browser_artifacts.why_web_only: There is no cursor on touch — the only signal that this is tappable disappears entirely
browser_artifacts.port_advice: Add a visible affordance (timestamp chip, underline, or pressed state) or the user will never discover click-to-seek

components.name: voice-selector
components.purpose: A searchable picker for a TTS voice, showing each voice's gender, accent, and age, with an audio preview per voice.
essential_behavior: CRITICAL: tapping VoiceSelectorPreview inside an item PLAYS the sample and must NOT select the voice. Two nested targets, two distinct outcomes
Preview has three states: play, playing (pause icon), loading (disabled)
VoiceSelectorAccent maps 30 lowercase accent keys to flag emoji; the lookup is CASE-SENSITIVE ('AMERICAN' renders nothing)
VoiceSelectorGender maps to icons; unknown values fall back rather than throwing
Type-to-filter with an explicit empty state

components.name: web-preview
components.purpose: Embeds a live preview of a URL the agent generated or is working on, with a URL bar, navigation, and a captured console.
essential_behavior: URL bar is editable: typing a URL and pressing Enter navigates and calls onUrlChange
WebPreviewBody ALWAYS carries a sandbox attribute — untrusted generated content is never given full privileges
A loading slot renders while the frame loads

browser_artifacts.artifact: <iframe> with the sandbox attribute

You must lock it down yourself: originWhitelist, javaScriptEnabled, allowFileAccess=false, allowsInlineMediaPlayback, and setSupportMultipleWindows(false). Treat this as a security task, not a rename

inherently_web_shaped.name: canvas
inherently_web_shaped.reason: It is @xyflow/react end to end: absolutely-positioned divs under a CSS transform matrix, SVG edge layer, wheel/pointer events, ResizeObserver and getBoundingClientRect node measurement. Nothing survives except the concept. A native version is react-native-gesture-handler + reanimated + react-native-svg and is a project of its own, not a port task. Recommend cutting it from MVP and shipping the other 42 first.

inherently_web_shaped.name: node
inherently_web_shaped.reason: The card body IS shadcn Card, and RNR ships Card — NodeHeader/NodeTitle/NodeDescription/NodeContent/NodeFooter port on day one. What does not port is `handles`, which only has meaning inside React Flow's coordinate store. Ship Node as a plain card; drop the handle prop unless canvas is rebuilt.

inherently_web_shaped.name: edge
inherently_web_shaped.reason: SVG bezier paths computed by React Flow's getBezierPath, animated by CSS/SMIL, with SVG <marker> arrowheads, rendered into React Flow's SVG layer. Meaningless without canvas. If canvas is ever rebuilt, this is react-native-svg Path + reanimated withRepeat — a rewrite, not a port.

inherently_web_shaped.name: connection
inherently_web_shaped.reason: It is a render-prop slot React Flow calls with live pointer coordinates during an edge drag. Both the caller and the coordinate space are absent in RN.

inherently_web_shaped.name: panel
inherently_web_shaped.reason: Technically a native substitute exists — it is an absolutely positioned View outside the transform layer — but that is roughly ten lines and only meaningful with canvas. Not worth a registry item on its own.

inherently_web_shaped.name: controls
inherently_web_shaped.reason: Zoom-in/zoom-out buttons acting on React Flow's viewport store. Discrete zoom buttons are a desktop idiom; on touch, pinch replaces them. Only fit-view would be worth keeping, and only if canvas exists.

inherently_web_shaped.name: toolbar
inherently_web_shaped.reason: @xyflow/react NodeToolbar — it places itself from the owning node's measured DOM rect and the viewport transform, and is composed inside a nodeTypes component. Also hover/selection-triggered. No standalone value.

inherently_web_shaped.name: web-preview
inherently_web_shaped.reason: react-native-webview is a genuine substitute for the iframe, and the URL bar / nav / console composition all port. Two caveats that must be planned, not assumed: (1) the iframe `sandbox` attribute has NO WebView equivalent — you must reproduce the isolation manually via originWhitelist, javaScriptEnabled, allowFileAccess, and blocking new windows; (2) console capture requires injectedJavaScriptBeforeContentLoaded + postMessage/onMessage rather than direct console patching.

inherently_web_shaped.name: jsx-preview
inherently_web_shaped.reason: react-jsx-parser parses a model-authored JSX string against HTML intrinsics. RN has no intrinsic elements, so an unmapped tag renders nothing at all — the component would silently show blank. It is also the highest-security-risk item in the set: on web the blast radius is a div, in an app it is your component tree. If it ships, it must be a strict allowlist interpreter mapping to View/Text/Image/RNR components with everything else rejected. Keep the streaming behaviors (auto-close unclosed tags, strip mid-attribute cutoffs, fall back to last-good JSX) — those are renderer-agnostic and are what stop the preview flashing.

inherently_web_shaped.name: sandbox
inherently_web_shaped.reason: The shell is only Collapsible + Tabs + a status badge, and RNR ships both primitives. Its risk is entirely inherited from code-block and terminal, not from the container. Narrow the tab bar to two tabs on phone.

inherently_web_shaped.name: terminal
inherently_web_shaped.reason: Substantial but tractable. ansi-to-react emits HTML spans and must be replaced with an ANSI tokenizer feeding nested <Text>. Everything else — auto-scroll, streaming cursor, clear/copy, the onClear-gates-the-button rule — ports directly. One design decision to make once: map the 16 ANSI colors onto RNR theme tokens so output is legible in light mode, rather than passing raw ANSI colors through.

inherently_web_shaped.name: artifact
inherently_web_shaped.reason: It is a header + actions + scrollable content shell with no web-specific machinery. The only real change is placement: on web it is a side panel next to the transcript; on a phone it must be a full-screen sheet or a pushed route. Also strip the hover-only tooltips on ArtifactAction.

inherently_web_shaped.name: file-tree
inherently_web_shaped.reason: Nested collapsibles, which RNR ships. Two things need genuine mobile design work rather than translation: (1) the chevron-expands / name-selects split lives in a ~24px row that a finger cannot resolve — either give each target ≥44pt or move one behavior to long-press, but do NOT merge them; (2) hover-revealed FileTreeActions become invisible on touch. Deep indent also needs capping or replacing with drill-down.

inherently_web_shaped.name: chart-shaped components
inherently_web_shaped.reason: CORRECTION for the port team: there is no chart component among the 49. `chart` appears only in the 55-primitive dependency list and NO AI Elements component in the inventory consumes it. The actual data visualization inside AI Elements is shadcn `progress` bars — in context (token usage), test-results (pass rate), and package-info — all of which RNR already ships. If you later port the shadcn `chart` primitive itself, note it is a thin wrapper over Recharts (SVG + DOM measurement + hover tooltips) with no RN path; that would be victory-vega/react-native-svg territory, and it is out of scope for this inventory.

inherently_web_shaped.name: persona
inherently_web_shaped.reason: Looks maximally web-shaped (WebGL2 canvas) but is the exception: it is Rive, and rive-react-native is a first-party runtime. The .riv asset, the six variants, and the five state-machine inputs port directly. The specific web bug (Strict Mode double-mount exhausting the WebGL context limit) does not exist in RN, though its lesson — do not create the runtime instance in a mount effect that can double-fire — still applies.

inherently_web_shaped.name: audio-player
inherently_web_shaped.reason: Built on media-chrome Web Components (MediaController, MediaPlayButton, MediaTimeRange…). Custom Elements do not exist in RN, so every control is a rewrite over expo-audio or react-native-track-player. Only the slot names and the seekOffset semantics survive. Also drop the volume slider — mobile OSes own volume.

inherently_web_shaped.name: speech-input
inherently_web_shaped.reason: Its primary engine is window.SpeechRecognition, a Chrome-only API. The MediaRecorder fallback also has no direct equivalent. Rebuild on expo-speech-recognition (on-device) or make the onAudioRecorded → server transcribe() path the only route. Keep two behaviors verbatim: only FINAL transcripts fire onTranscriptionChange, and with no engine available the button is disabled rather than fake-listening.

inherently_web_shaped.name: mic-selector
inherently_web_shaped.reason: Built on navigator.mediaDevices.enumerateDevices(). iOS and Android deliberately do not expose an arbitrary audio-input device list to apps — the platform owns routing via AVAudioSession / Bluetooth. There is no honest native equivalent. Either drop it or replace it with a system route picker, which is a different component with a different API.

inherently_web_shaped.name: model-selector / voice-selector
inherently_web_shaped.reason: Both are cmdk Command palettes in a Dialog. cmdk is DOM-only and `command` is in the 26-component RNR gap list, so you will build the primitive once: bottom sheet + sectioned FlatList + TextInput filter, and reuse it for both. Drop the ⌘K shortcut slots. Preserve voice-selector's law that preview PLAYS and does not select — and give that nested button a real touch target.

types_touched: UIMessage (NOT ConversationMessage — that name was removed in 1.9.0)
ToolUIPart and DynamicToolUIPart (exported together as ToolPart)
ToolUIPart fields consumed: type, state, input, output, errorText, toolCallId, approval
LanguageModelUsage ({ inputTokens, outputTokens, reasoningTokens, cachedInputTokens }) for context
speech Result ({ base64, mediaType }) for audio-player
transcribe() segments ({ text, startSecond, endSecond }) for transcription
ai_sdk_seam.notes: This union is the ONE place where AI Elements and the AI SDK already line up with zero adapter — <ToolHeader state={part.state}> type-checks against a UIMessage tool part directly. Preserve it verbatim in the port; a hand-rolled status union type-checks locally and silently drifts on the next SDK upgrade. Badge mapping is fixed: input-streaming→Pending, input-available→Running, output-available→Completed, output-error→Error, approval-requested→Awaiting Approval, approval-responded→Responded, output-denied→Denied. Two states are usually skipped and should be planned deliberately: (a) input-streaming renders while the model is still emitting arguments, so ToolInput must survive partial/invalid JSON and it is the shortest-lived state and therefore the most likely to be visually broken; (b) approval-requested/approval-responded are the human-in-the-loop path — without a real UI and a real response call (addToolApprovalResponse({ id, approved })) a gated agent silently stalls forever. Route-side flags matter: reasoning parts only exist with toUIMessageStreamResponse({ sendReasoning: true }), and source parts only with sendSources: true — a port team that sees no reasoning/sources is looking at a route gap, not a component bug. Finally: NONE of these 49 files call a model, own message state, or implement retry/abort/persistence. They are views over state you own (useChat or equivalent). The RN port inherits that boundary exactly — and inherits two responsibilities the web components never had to carry: keyboard avoidance and safe-area insets around the composer, and virtualization of the transcript.
